claims.text: Replacing alumina with cerium oxide as the support improves automotive exhaust catalyst activity.
Replacing alumina with cerium oxide as the support improves automotive exhaust catalyst durability.
Replacing alumina with cerium oxide enables reduced platinum-group-metal consumption relative to alumina-supported catalysts.
The proposed benefits hold under cyclic-redox automotive exhaust operation at roughly 200–800 °C and near-stoichiometric air–fuel ratios.
Cerium oxide provides enhanced oxygen-storage capability compared with alumina.
Cerium oxide provides enhanced redox-cycling capability compared with alumina.
The cerium oxide support helps maintain platinum-group-metal dispersion.
The cerium oxide support prevents or inhibits platinum-group-metal nanoparticle sintering.
Cerium oxide acts as an oxygen reservoir that transfers oxygen to active platinum-group-metal sites.
Inhibition of nanoparticle sintering and thermal degradation by cerium oxide improves catalyst durability.
Oxygen transfer from cerium oxide to platinum-group-metal sites improves catalytic kinetics.
Cerium-oxide-supported catalysts will have lower light-off temperatures than conventional alumina-supported catalysts.
Cerium-oxide-supported catalysts will have higher pollutant conversion efficiencies than conventional alumina-supported catalysts.
Cerium-oxide-supported catalysts will have better long-term stability than conventional alumina-supported catalysts.
The activity and durability gains will permit lower platinum-group-metal loading without compromising performance.
Performance gains may diminish under extreme thermal conditions or exposure to contaminated fuel.
